purpose: Instructions for creating and maintaining DSA problem pages in the Notion DSA Problems database.
source_of_truth: This file is the authoritative structure for Notion DSA pages. Existing good pages may be used as visual references, but this spec overrides older mistakes.

database.name: DSA Problems
rules: Do not repeat Problem URL or GitHub URL inside the page body because they already exist as database properties.
Create the full solution note directly inside the database row/page.
Use only valid existing Study Patterns unless the database schema is intentionally updated.

pre_creation_checks: Check whether the problem already exists in the DSA Problems database.
Open 1-2 correctly formatted existing DSA pages as references.
Read all provided GitHub solution files for the problem.
Research authoritative external sources for established alternative solutions even when those solutions are not present in the GitHub repository.
Identify whether genuine Brute Force, Better, and Optimal approaches exist in the wider problem-solving literature; do not treat the repository as the complete approach inventory.
Do not blindly copy old formatting errors from reference pages.

solution_selection_rules.provided_solution: Always preserve and include any solution already provided in the GitHub repo.
solution_selection_rules.other_solutions: Use external research to include other established brute-force, better, or optimal approaches when they add educational or interview value, even if the user has not implemented them in the repository.
solution_selection_rules.labeling: Do not assume the provided solution is optimal. Label each approach by what it actually is.
solution_selection_rules.progression_rule: When multiple complexity levels exist, their physical order on the page must be Brute Force -> Better -> Optimal. No other ordering is acceptable. Omit a level only when no genuine approach exists; never place an earlier level after a later one.
solution_selection_rules.progression_explanation: When multiple approaches exist, add a How to Improve the Approach section that explains the observation, bottleneck, and data-structure or algorithm change that transforms Brute Force into Better and Better into Optimal.
solution_selection_rules.approach_format: Write every Approach section as a clear numbered list of steps rather than a prose paragraph.
solution_selection_rules.data_structure_explanation: For every approach, explicitly name the data structure or structures used, explain what each one stores, and state why each structure fits the algorithm.
solution_selection_rules.equal_treatment_for_alternatives: Every added alternative solution must be explained with the same depth as the repository solution. Never use abbreviated, lazy, or summary-only Approach, Code Explanation, Dry Run, or Complexity sections.

page_structure.heading: Problem
page_structure.content: Short faithful explanation of the problem.

rules: Use a good non-trivial example that exposes the important behavior of the algorithm.
Prefer examples that demonstrate edge cases, state changes, or the key invariant.
Explicitly show how every important data structure changes or is used during the dry run.
Use visual tables/boxes for arrays, pointers, hash maps, stacks, queues, and trees when helpful.
Do not use trivial one-element examples unless the problem specifically requires them.

notion_table_rule.required: Use real Notion table syntax, never escaped table text.

style.explanation_depth: Elaborate the intuition, approach, code explanation, and dry run in simple language so a learner can follow why each step works, while avoiding unnecessary repetition.
code_source_priority: Use canonical/optimal solution as final approach when appropriate

post_creation_checks: Verify tables render as actual Notion tables.
Verify the dry run uses a strong example.
